C-INFRA-CI-BASELINE-20260828.Summary: Implement Phase A and the minimum repository-owned portion of Phase B from the Worldline CI/CD policy.
C-INFRA-CI-BASELINE-20260828.Problem: Worldline has pinned Rust and local verification commands but no repository-owned CI entrypoint, stable required check topology, workflow permissions contract, or machine-enforced architecture and proving-slice gates.

Goals.Goal: Create a local cross-platform CI entrypoint that owns source, correctness, architecture-security, and proving-slice suites.
Create minimal GitHub pull-request and master workflows whose stable jobs call only repository-owned verification logic.
Make GRACE integrity, kernel dependency direction, EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC, and permanent S0 and S1 proving evidence explicit gates.
Document branch-protection check names and failure ownership without claiming external repository settings were applied.

Constraints.Constraint: docs/CI-CD.md is the living engineering policy and this change must implement only its Phase A plus the minimum repository-owned Phase B envelope.
GitHub Actions is orchestration only; all required verification logic must run locally.
Rust 1.98.0 and workflow actions must be pinned; workflow permissions must default to read-only.
Required gates may not use continue-on-error, silent test discovery loss, or success by skipping.
No production Rust source or protected acceptance test may be modified by this change.
Existing unrelated dirty-tree work is coexistence state and must not be claimed, reformatted, reverted, or absorbed.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Nightly fuzzing, Miri, sanitizers, chaos, long-running concurrency suites, and performance baselines.
Application packaging, signing, SBOM publication, attestations, automatic deployment, or a release workflow that publishes artifacts.
Changing GitHub branch-protection settings through an external API.
Adding live browser, model-provider, network-service, or production-credential tests.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A repository-owned PowerShell entrypoint exposes stable source, correctness, architecture-security, proving-slice, and all suites and returns nonzero on every failed required command.

Pull-request and master workflows use stable job names, pinned actions, minimal permissions, concurrency cancellation where appropriate, the pinned project toolchain, and no duplicated verification business logic.
The source suite runs rustfmt, cargo check, Clippy with warnings denied, and rustdoc; correctness runs the workspace tests.
The architecture-security suite validates the GRACE model and kernel dependency direction and executes the current security, lifecycle, state, and RPC-event acceptance evidence.
The proving-slice suite runs the reference boundary acceptance test and worldline-demo so S0 and S1 remain permanent gates.
README and repository templates identify the local command and exact required check names while explicitly distinguishing local evidence from an actual hosted CI run.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: All repository-owned gates pass locally; GRACE final lint passes; workflow syntax and immutable action references are inspectable. Hosted CI remains unverified until a named GitHub run exists.

Assumptions.Assumption: The default integration branch is master and GitHub Actions is the intended hosted orchestrator.
The user's 2026-08-28 instruction and supplied CI/CD policy explicitly approve this normative spec; the executable plan remains separately draft until approved.
